evidence.title: Consultant performance gains depend on task fit, and coherence need not mean correctness
evidence.observation: Source-reported finding: Dell’Acqua and colleagues report randomized task experiments with 758 BCG consultants. On an 18-task workflow within the tested capability frontier, GPT-4 access increased task completion and quality while reducing time. On a separate complex managerial task, assisted participants were faster but less often correct; even incorrect assisted answers received higher coherence ratings. Observation context: 2023 GPT-4 study context; precise execution dates not established in this inspection.
evidence.evidence_standing: Author-reported bounded study; not independently reproduced by the Commons
evidence.glossary_fit: Illustrative or qualifying comparison; founding definitions and classifications unchanged
evidence.limitations: One firm, mostly early-career consultants, constructed tasks and June 2023 GPT-4. One outside-frontier task cannot establish a general boundary. Speed, coherence and correctness are separate measures. Findings are paired settings within one study, not independent replications. The preregistration omitted the later jagged-frontier framing and detailed task descriptions.
evidence.open_questions: Which results transfer to other populations, tool versions, longer periods and operational governance settings? No such transfer is established by inclusion.
evidence.support_assessment: Commons interpretation: Speed and persuasive coherence can diverge from correctness. Reduced task barriers depended on task/model fit.
evidence.dispute_status: See recorded source-version qualifications and finding limits; no systematic clearance claimed.

terms.name: Constraint compression
terms.definition: A reduction, often AI-enabled, in the practical barriers of knowledge, expertise, labor, cost, time, or coordination that once limited an activity. It describes the change in constraints, not the eventual impact of the activity.

terms.name: Outcome–purpose divergence
terms.definition: A condition in which meeting an immediate objective or metric degrades the benefit or purpose that justified pursuing it. The divergence can occur through narrow measures or indirect consequences without an intent to deceive.
